title: Cascade - Embeddings & Rerank Discovery
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Discovery call with Cascade Analytics to understand current retrieval pipeline (Elastic + in-house FAISS), discuss Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private options for embedding storage and reranking, evaluate throughput targets (QPS and tail latency), discuss dimensionality (1536 vs 768 vs 128) and hybrid BM25+ANN approaches, and agree next steps to run a small benchmark and share security docs and pricing.
action_items: Alex Chen: Share Redwood hosted pricing and Dedicated commitment tiers (due 2026-07-17)
Samira Patel: Draft benchmark plan and list of sample queries to run (due 2026-07-20)
Maya Thompson: Provide sample dataset export (100k rows) and current EV metrics (due 2026-07-18)
Liam O'Connor: Confirm network egress constraints and VPC peering possibilities (due 2026-07-21)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated sizing options
Customer to drop sample export to S3 and share query patterns
Schedule 1-hr technical bench with SEs to run embedding + rerank microbench (week of 7/20)
Send SOC2 & security questionnaire and KMS/HSM integration notes
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, with Samira and Diego on the call. How's everyone doing?
00:10 Jin (Cascade): Hi Alex, thanks. I'm Jin, Head of Search at Cascade. We are exploring better rerank for our product search, current infra is Elastic + some in-house FAISS indexes, curious what Redwood offers.
00:20 Samira (Redwood SE): quick intro from me - I focus on embeddings/rerank and infra. Would love to hear about your current workflow and pain points.
00:30 Maya (Cascade): Sure. We generate 1536-dim embeddings using a public model, store vectors in FAISS on EC2. Retrieval is hybrid: BM25 to filter then ANN rerank. Problems: tail latency spikes, cost for big indexes, also experiments with lower-dim embeddings to save cost but worried about quality drop.
00:48 Alex: Great, that aligns with many customers. Quick clarifying Qs: what's your 95th ms target for search rerank? and what's QPS?
00:55 Jin: For UI search we'd like < 200ms P95, QPS around 30 steady but peaks to 150 during campaigns. We also have API endpoints that need lower latency.
01:10 Samira: Sounds reasonable. Two levers: model/dim size and deployment mode. Hosted Redwood API can be easiest to start, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved GPU pools, Private (VPC) for if you have compliance needs. Any constraints on data residency/SSO?
01:28 Liam (Cascade): We need SSO (SAML) and SOC2 docs, and would prefer VPC peering for dedicated traffic if possible. We also have encryption keys in AWS KMS.
01:36 Diego (Redwood): We support SAML SSO and can integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we provide controls and SOC2, and we can sign an NDA. For VPC peering we have options in Redwood Dedicated or Private.
01:48 Maya: Another question: storage of embeddings - do you host vectors in your system or do we keep them in our DB and call Redwood for scoring?
01:58 Samira: Both patterns are common. Hosted Redwood can store vectors for you (managed vector store) for convenience, or you can keep vectors in your DB and call our scorer/endpoint for rerank. With Dedicated we can co-locate the vector store on the same GPU fleet to reduce egress and latency.
02:15 Jin: What about Vector DB compatibility - Pinecone, Milvus etc - how does Redwood integrate?
02:22 Samira: We have connectors and common export/import formats; many customers use Pinecone, Milvus, or FAISS. For a high QPS tail, we often recommend Dedicated with local ANN (HNSW/IVF) tuned per index. We can also provide an embeddings-only hosted endpoint and you keep index in Milvus.
02:42 Maya: There's also cost; trying to understand interplay of dimensionality and cost. We currently use 1536 dims. If we drop to 768 or 512, how much improvement do you usually see?
02:55 Samira: tradeoffs: roughly linear-ish for storage and memory, but latency improvements depend on index type and quantization. For example, switching to 768 can cut index memory maybe ~2x relative to 1536, and quantization (OPQ+PQ) can further reduce size by 4x with some accuracy tradeoff. Fine-tuning can retain quality. We typically run recall/ndcg evals on a holdout set to measure.
03:18 Jin: Do you support hybrid search - BM25 + ANN in one flow?
03:22 Samira: Yes, hybrid is standard: initial BM25 filter then ANN rerank on the reduced set. Redwood's routing supports that; we also have built-in caching for prefixes/queries to speed up common queries.
03:36 Maya: How about throughput - we need to sustain bursts up to 150 QPS with low tail latency. Can Dedicated handle that without huge cost?
03:44 Diego: Dedicated is designed for predictable throughput. We size GPU pools based on your tail QPS and target latency. There are autoscaling policies and burst capacity, and we can propose a commit that balances cost and spare capacity. For short bursts, burst pools are cheaper than provisioning for peak constantly.
03:58 Jin: Any benchmarks? and can you run a proof-of-concept?
04:02 Alex: Yes, we can run a POC. Typical POCs include: we ask for a 50k-200k sample, you give us queries, we run end-to-end with your embeddings and with our hosted/dedicated configs and share latency and recall curves. Samira will lead the tech bench.
04:18 Maya: About model orchestration - we sometimes use multiple embedding models for different content types. Can Redwood handle variable dimensionality across documents?
04:26 Samira: Yes, but it's more efficient to standardize dims per index. We can host separate indexes per model/dim, and Redwood routing can pick the right index. Mixing dims inside a single ANN index is not recommended.
04:40 Liam: Networking - for Private deployment, do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink? Egress charges are a concern.
04:48 Diego: We support VPC peering and private connectivity on Dedicated/Private plans. For Hosted, egress is typically via secure HTTPS with encryption in transit; depending on volume, egress costs could be material and customers often prefer Dedicated if egress is a big concern.
05:02 Jin: Security - we need audit logs and key rotation. What logging retention does Redwood provide?
05:08 Alex: We have per-request tracing and audit logs in the Console; retention depends on plan, with enterprise add-ons for longer retention. KMS integration for encryption-at-rest is available for Private. We'll share the SOC2 and logging docs.
05:20 Maya: A slightly technical Q - how do you handle KV cache and attention caching for rerank? We sometimes do many short requests with overlapping prefixes.
05:29 Samira: Our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching optimizations. For rerank (short contexts), batch inference and dynamic batching are key. We can tune batch windows to meet latency SLOs while improving throughput. Note: sometimes the transcript phrase K-V cache is mis-spoken as kay-vee cash - apologies for my accent.
05:49 Jin: Any constraints on approximate algorithms - HNSW vs IVF vs PQ? Which do you pick?
05:55 Samira: Choice depends on vector dim and recall vs latency target. HNSW is good for low-latency and good recall at moderate scale; IVF+PQ can be more memory efficient at huge scale but adds recall complexity. We'll help recommend based on your eval.
06:10 Maya: We also have embeddings refresh every night, index rebuilding takes time; can Redwood do incremental updates?
06:16 Diego: Yes, we support incremental indexing and background rebuilds; for large reimports we recommend a zero-downtime swap strategy.
06:26 Jin: How do you measure rerank quality? We use NDCG@10 and MRR. Is that supported?
06:31 Samira: Absolutely, our eval kit computes NDCG, MRR, precision@k etc. We can run your metrics and surface regressions in Redwood Optimize.
06:40 Maya: Quick note - we also evaluate embedding dimension projection (PCA) on-device to speed up things. Does Redwood support custom preprocessing?
06:48 Samira: You can supply preprocessed embeddings; Redwood doesn't force you to compute them. For hosted embedding generation we also support webhooks and custom model hosting if you want control.
06:58 Jin: Great. Cost model - how is hosted charged? per-token and per-embedding? We need an estimate for 100M vectors.
07:06 Alex: Hosted embeddings are per-embedding unit; storage and query units can be metered. For 100M vectors storage and query cost could be material; many customers move to Dedicated/Private for large-scale indexes to reduce per-query cost. We'll produce an estimate in the follow-up pricing doc.
07:22 Maya: Competitor question - some teams use Pinecone with a caching layer. What differentiates Redwood?
07:28 Alex: We focus on production-grade inference with routing, dedidcated GPU pools, and integrated rerank + generation capabilities. Also transparent perf benchmarks, and ops features like rollouts, canaries, and trace-level billing.
07:44 Jin: Anything else we should be aware of on the technical side?
07:48 Samira: Just that we typically recommend a small baseline test: 50k sample, run host/dedicated bench, compare dims and PQ settings, and measure recall and latency. Also run hybrid BM25 cutoff thresholds to find sweet spot for candidates.
08:02 Maya: Sounds good. Let's talk timeline: we'd like to run a bench next week if possible.
08:06 Alex: We can do that - Samira will send a benchmark plan and we'll schedule a 60-minute SE bench.
08:12 Jin: Perfect. Any docs you plan to share?
08:15 Alex: We'll send SOC2, security questionnaire, pricing tiers, and a dedicated POC plan.
08:20 Maya: Quick note on instrumentation - we want per-query latency breakdowns and token-level cost.
08:26 Diego: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and per-route metrics, and we can set retention/alerts.
08:34 Jin: Alright, let's recap.
08:36 Alex: Recap: Redwood to send pricing + SOC2; Samira to send bench plan; customer to provide 50-200k sample export and query set; schedule tech bench week of 7/20. Anything to add?
08:50 Jin: No, that covers it. Thanks everyone.
08:52 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up.
09:00 End of recording

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors present (product names slightly misspelled in the auto transcript, e.g., "dedidcated" for Dedicated; some acronyms like VPC sometimes transcribed as V-P-C). There is some crosstalk at times and filler words preserved.
